summary: Surama Dasgupta worked in philosophy and Indology. She completed her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Calcutta and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Cambridge around 1948–1950.

Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Tribhuvan University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta and University of Cambridge. He held professorships at Chittagong College, Presidency University, and Calcutta, and served as Principal of Sanskrit College (~1931–1942).

Suryya Kumar Bhuyan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, the University of Calcutta, and Presidency University, Kolkata, later serving as a professor at Cotton University from circa 1918 to 1946.

Susan Andrews is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University (~2007–2013) under Chun-fang Yu, having also studied under Bernard Faure, David Max Moerman, Michael Como, Koichi Shinohara, and Phyllis Granoff.

Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004. Her teachers included Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.
Susan L. Beningson specializes in sinology, history, and archaeology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 2009, with Stephen F. Teiser and Vidya Dehejia serving on her committee.
Susan Naquin is a historian and sinologist. She served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1976 to 1993 and held a post at Princeton University from circa 1993 to 2013.

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard University and the Free University of Berlin. She held academic positions at Yale University (~1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (~1996–2000), and joined the Einstein Forum around 2000.

Susan Whitfield specializes in history, archaeology, sinology, and Central Asian studies. After studying at SOAS University of London, she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and held a post at the University of East Anglia (~2018).

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph worked in Indology and related fields. She studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University, later holding posts at Harvard (~1955–1964) and the University of Chicago (~1964–2002).

Susanne Mrozik works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Harvard under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles, later holding posts at Western Michigan University (~1998–2001) and Mount Holyoke College (~2001).

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, later serving there as a lecturer in 1986 and as Lecturer in Indian Religions at the University of Birmingham.

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002) under Makio Takemura, and has served as a lecturer at Hanazono University, Bukkyo University, and Kyoto University.
Susumu Sakurabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University, where he later served as a professor from circa 1968 to 1996.

Susumu Shimazono works in religious studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1982–1987), the University of Tokyo (~1994–2013), and Sophia University (~2013–2021).

Susumu Yamaguchi specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani, Kyoto, and Paris universities under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin, serving as a professor at Otani University from 1922 to 1976.
Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Nalanda College (~1946–1955) and held posts at the University of Toronto and the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies.
Suzanne Karpelès was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1917 to 1922 and held a post at the French Information Bureau.

Suzanne Newcombe is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She earned her doctorate at Cambridge, held posts at Inform and LSE (~2001–2015), and became a senior lecturer at the Open University (~2015) and honorary director at King's College London (~2018).
